messages.subject: Specifying a mirt model using contents of SingleGroupClass object
messages.subject_clean: Specifying a mirt model using contents of SingleGroupClass object
messages.body_plain:
Hi Phil et al,

Let's say we have:

###
data <- expand.table(LSAT7)
mod1 <- mirt(data, 1)
###

I want to now fit the same model specified in the above call to mirt() but using new data. If one is familiar with the update() function, what I want is to basically do something akin to:

###
data2 <- data[-1,] #remove first row
mod2 <- update(mod1,data=data2) #doesn't actually work
###

where mod2 will have the same IRT model estimated in the original call to mirt (which yielded mod1) but now applied to data2. Essentially, I want to reconstruct the oroiginal call to mirt() using the elements of the SingleGroupClass object mod1.

My sense is that everything one would need to do it is contained in the mod1 object. You can get, for example, itemtype info:

###
mod1@Model$itemtype
###

but I can't see a way of easily repackaging all the relevant information. Is there an efficient way of doing this (e.g., I had hoped there might be a function which converted elements of mod1 into a model specification object along the lines of what is returned by mirt.model)? Thanks in advance for any help and, while I searched the archives, apologies if I missed a previous post on this.

Ben

PS-Another thought I had was to use the information in mod1@Call, but I think that elements of that would need to be parsed in the same environment as the original call and I don't think that would work in the generic case I have in mind.

messages.subject_clean: Specifying a mirt model using contents of SingleGroupClass object
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ben,

Not quite sure if this is what you're looking for, but using home-grown functions on the fly are pretty good for this type of thing. Here's an example:

########
library(mirt)
data <- expand.table(LSAT7)
mod1 <- mirt(data)

my_mirt <- function(index, data, ...){
    dd <- data[-index, , drop=FALSE]
    mod <- mirt(dd, ...)
    mod
}

mods <- sapply(seq(1,1000, by=100), my_mirt,
               data=data, itemtype = '3PL')
lapply(mods, coef, simplify=TRUE)
#####

Functions like update() would be nice but AFAIK they are only useful when the input is a simple formula type. HTH for now.

Phil

messages.body_plain:
Hi Phil,

Thanks for the response! My definition of data2 may have been misleading; the removal of the first row was just to motivate data2 as a 'novel' dataset. The real goal is to be able to completely specify the non-data parts of the second call to mirt() using the elements stored in the first call. To better motivate what I want, consider:

###

library(mirt)
data <- expand.table(LSAT7)
mod1 <- mirt(data)

mod2 <- mirt(data[-1,],itemtype=mod1@Model$itemtype)

###

The goal would be to specify a call as in the assignment to mod2 that replicates the model specified in mod1. It's simple here given that we fit a very simple model, but I'm trying to figure out a way of handling the generic case where the specification in mod1 may be much more complex. It might be that such functionality is not yet implemented; even knowing that is the case would be useful.

Thanks! Ben

# Fit the initial GRSM model
model_grsm <- mirt(Science, 1, itemtype = "grsm")

> coef(model_grsm, simplify=TRUE)
$items
                     a1        b1       b2        b3      c

Future       1.245 3.549 1.683 -0.955 -0.294
Benefit      1.114 3.549 1.683 -0.955 -0.683

# Extract the parameters

pars

# Modify the parameter values to fix a1 to 1
pars$value[pars$name == "a1"] <- 1  # Fix slopes to 1
values$est[values$name == "a1"] <- FALSE

# Refit the model with the modified parameters [ERROR]
fixed_model <- mirt(Science, model = 1, pars = pars)

Error: Rows in supplied and starting value data.frame objects do not match. Were the
             data or itemtype input arguments modified?

============================================================

Assuming once I get the parameters from the fixed model, how should I translate the constrained GRSM into the standard GRM in mirtCAT()?
Something like the below?

# extract coefficients
params_grsm =coef(fixed_model, simplify=TRUE)

# Adjust the b values by distributing the shift parameter c
params_grm <- params_grsm$items

# For each item, adjust the b values
for (i in 1:nrow(params_grm)) {
  params_grm[i, "b1"] <- params_grm[i, "b1"] - params_grm[i, "c"]
  params_grm[i, "b2"] <- params_grm[i, "b2"] - params_grm[i, "c"]
  params_grm[i, "b3"] <- params_grm[i, "b3"] - params_grm[i, "c"]
}

# Remove the shift parameter c from the model (as it is now incorporated into the b values)
params_grm <- params_grm[, !colnames(params_grm) %in% "c"]
print(params_grm)

# Estimate the theta scores for all respondents
theta_scores <- fscores(fixed_model)

# Calculate the variance of the theta scores
VAR_theta <- var(theta_scores)

# Adjust thresholds by incorporating VAR(theta)
thresholds <- grep("^b", colnames(params_grm))
params_grm[, thresholds] <- params_grm[, thresholds] * as.vector(sqrt(VAR_theta))

# Create mirtCAT object with adjusted itempool and theta prior
# Where can i include VAR(theta) in the mirtCAT function? I've rescaled the slopes by incorporating VAR(theta) above, so maybe I don't have to do this step anymore?
mirtCAT_object <- mirtCAT(mo = itempool,
                          model = rep("graded", nrow(itempool)),
                          method = "MAP",
                          criteria = "MEPV",
                          theta_range = c(-6, 6))

Thanks for your help!
Aiden

messages.subject: 'mirt' or 'multipleGroup' function for Vertical Equating?
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I’m currently working on a vertical equating process. I have data from 20 math items administered to third-grade students and another set of 20 math items given to fourth-grade students. I also have six anchor items that were answered by students from both grades.

These six anchor items come from a different test used in large-scale assessments in Brazil. Therefore, besides placing the third and fourth-grade scores on the same scale, I also want to fix the anchor items to the parameters obtained from the original sample in which they were originally calibrated. In summary,  along with performing concurrent calibration to equate the scores of third and fourth grades, I also intend to fix the parameters of the anchor items to ensure that the estimated scores are scaled based on the sample in which these six items were originally tested.

My questions are as follows:
In this scenario, would it be more appropriate to use the 'mirt' function or the 'multipleGroup' function? Take into account that the parameters for the six anchor items will not be constrained across groups but fixed at known values.
For vertical equating, what is the best approach? Should I use the 'mirt' function and fix the parameters of the anchor items so they are not estimated (est = FALSE), or should I use the 'multipleGroup' function and set these items as anchors (constrained across groups)? What is the difference between the two approaches?

messages.subject: Re: 'mirt' or 'multipleGroup' function for Vertical Equating?
messages.body_plain:
UPDATE: I conducted the scaling on mydata using the 'multipleGroup' function, again fixing the anchor item parameters at known values. The coefficient estimates were extremely close to those obtained with the 'mirt' function. I fixed the slopes and intercepts as invariant. The mean of the factor scores for both grades was nearly identical to those obtained from the single-group analysis. As expected, the mean scores for the fourth grade were substantially higher, and the mean scores for the third grade were lower, whether using the 'mirt' function or 'multipleGroup'. Overall, both methods provided very similar results. However, I am still curious about the differences between them and which might be more suitable for vertical scaling.

On the other hand, when I use the 'multipleGroup' function and free the means and variances to be estimated, the mean scores for the third and fourth grades become very close, with almost no difference. I'm not sure why this is happening...
